trigger: Resource Ledger for the C++ diff (round 1 and Gate 8 passes 1 and 2)
classification_rationale: informational attestation, not a defect
summary: Resource Ledger: the range adds no owning raw resource (no fd, HANDLE, socket, FILE*, sqlite handle, OpenSSL or BCrypt object, thread, subprocess or temp path). The only lifetime-bearing items are borrowed const ForensicsPluginSet pointers (the set is a ServerImpl member declared before every borrower and immutable after boot), value-type ResponseTierFilter copies, std::function members capturing server state, a function-local RefusalLogThrottle and test-only RAII fixtures; every one is proven in the cpp-safety reports (cpp-safety.md and cpp-safety-p2.md under the run scratch directory). Informational attestation, not a defect; the policy floor for a Resource Ledger omission is satisfied by this row. Range note: the pre-rebase heads 08af0976b, 6e500efd5 and a5595d173 are tree-identical to their post-rebase equivalents 250319c56, fd41b7e59 and 7613b711a (message-only rebase).

trigger: a Forensics-tier plugin response arrives while any authenticated dashboard session is subscribed to the legacy live output stream
classification_rationale: the shared live output stream had no read tier at all, a missing control
summary: The legacy dashboard live output stream is shared by every session and carried rendered rows of Forensics-tier plugins to any subscriber. Pre-existing sibling of the original defect, surfaced because the diff made every stored-response reader take a tier. The fix publishes no row of a Forensics-tier plugin and, when the plugin set is unwired, no output row at all. Also raised as: arch-1 (architect; shown sec-1, not independent). Fixed by: fix(events): do not publish Forensics-tier plugin rows to the live output stream (2e7f73f99). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a policy whose check instruction names a Forensics-tier plugin
classification_rationale: a code comment stated such plugins are never operator-facing while the control branch contradicted it
summary: The policy evaluator read a check stored output through an unrestricted internal read and kept a bounded copy that the compliance routes and MCP serve below the Forensics tier; a new comment said such plugins are never operator-facing, which was false. Derived CRITICAL (I1 with E2), native HIGH; the derivation was not moved. The fix reads with the Forensics plugins excluded so a Forensics check scores unknown and stores no output, and corrects the comment. A separate follow-up (#6065) tracks the dispatch-side authorization of policy checks; it is not part of this finding fix. Copies stored before the upgrade are tracked as g8p2-comp-1a and g8p2-comp-1a-residual. Also raised as: cpx-1 (cpp-expert), arch-3 policy-evaluator part (architect), comp-3 (compliance-officer, HIGH if unfixed: the copy sat outside retention and erasure); all echoes were shown sec-2 and are not independent. Fixed by: fix(compliance): score a Forensics-plugin policy check unknown instead of reading its output (ec068391a). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a Forensics-tier plugin command ends with failure text that the tracker stores and publishes
classification_rationale: the execution tracker failure-text path had no tier, a missing control
summary: Per-agent failure text stored by the execution tracker reached the durable column, the event outbox, the execution bus, the executions drawer and MCP execution status for any Execution:Read holder, a lower tier than the plugin rows. Content volume from these plugins is unknown, hence native MEDIUM and derived HIGH. The fix keeps only a bounded machine token (or a fixed placeholder) at write and again at read for rows still inside the 24 hour command correlation. Residuals are tracked as g8-sec-1 (sibling sinks, fixed), UP-15 and g8-up-4. Also raised as: sec-6 (security-guardian, native LOW, first noted), sre-6 (sre, derived HIGH: write-side blanking leaves durable rows and the 24 hour outbox replay). Fixed by: fix(executions): keep only a bounded token as a Forensics plugin's tracker error text (101dfc09b). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a bundle with a Forensics-tier step polled by a caller who holds a dispatch approval but not Forensics:Read; a result set built from a Forensics execution
classification_rationale: two operator-visible readers were classified internal and had no tier
summary: Bundle collation and the result-set materialiser were classified as internal consumers with no read tier although their results reach operators (bundle output through REST and MCP, set membership computed from output content). Derived HIGH (I1), native MEDIUM. Owner ruling: a dispatch approval does not imply read, and a result set sourced from a Forensics execution materialises empty for every creator. Bundle collation later also audits as response.forensics.read (surface=bundle). Also raised as: arch-3 bundle and materialiser parts (architect, derived HIGH), cons-9 (consistency-auditor parity note). Fixed by: fix(bundles): apply the caller's Forensics tier when collating bundle output (047064217); fix(result-sets): never derive materialised membership from Forensics-plugin rows (4626c2bb9); feat(responses): bundle collation audits a served Forensics step as response.forensics.read (bfa085746). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: the authorization or management-group read fails while the Forensics tier is resolved for an otherwise authorized caller
classification_rationale: the degrade produced a plausible result with no signal, a missing signal
summary: The first resolver turned any scoped-read failure into a present-empty set, so an authorized caller received a 200 with Forensics rows silently missing and no marker or metric naming the surface. The fix is a tri-state resolver: an unresolved decision answers a retryable 503 (REST, legacy), a retryable internal error (MCP) or a visible notice (dashboard surfaces), counts yuzu_server_forensics_tier_withheld_total{reason}, logs a throttled WARN and raises the YuzuForensicsTierUnresolved alert. One owner-disclosed exception remains (UP2-3). Also raised as: sre-1 (sre, derived HIGH; shown UP-1). Fixed by: fix(responses): answer 503 when the Forensics visibility cannot be resolved (62c560f5e); feat(observability): count and alert on withheld Forensics-tier reads (941e51e48). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: the executions drawer is opened while the authorization read degrades, or by a token session
classification_rationale: the notice and the comment named the wrong cause and the wrong probe
summary: The drawer used the loud global-only Response:Read probe and, on a degrade, told the operator the permission was required, concealing the real state; it also wrote a denial row per refresh for cookie sessions and ignored management-group confinement for scoped holders. The fix uses the quiet fleet-read probe, a distinct notice for an unconfirmed decision and no store read on a denial. Also raised as: sec-4 (security-guardian, native MEDIUM), arch-5 (architect). Fixed by: fix(executions): quiet Response:Read probe on the drawer, with its own notice on a degrade (10b88f2bf). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

Fixed by: fix(hardware): permission notice on the result poll instead of a false timeout (f5afa58ae); test(hardware): a grant withdrawn between two polls ends the poll with the permission notice (8856797e9). Owner-accepted trade (UP-1: fail closed, never a partial 200); also the cost of KEEP in g8-arch-2 (e). Mitigation: resolve lazily, a negative cache per principal per generation, or treat ScopeReadFailed as Denied for callers with no scoped assignment. REVISIT TRIGGER: any production incident where a management-group store fault blocks ordinary response reads. Also raised as: UP2-4, g8-arch-4, g8-ch-3 (chaos-injector, live-fault shapes).

trigger: sustained dispatch above about 5000 recorded commands per hour (the reap cap is 5000 rows per pass at about 60 minute cadence), or a failing correlation reap, while a list, drawer or status read carries a failed execution
classification_rationale: an unindexed scan on a table whose reaper has a drain ceiling, extending a shared-pool lease
summary: The read-side scrub scans command_execution (no execution_id index) once per tracker read that has non-empty error text: 38 to 88 ms at 1M rows, 263 to 628 ms at 10M, linear in the table. The reviewer corrected the premise "bounded by the 24 hour reaper": the reaper drains at most about 120,000 rows per day, so above about 1.4 recorded commands per second the table grows without bound and the new scan turns disk growth into read latency; a capped pass is invisible. Native LOW, derived MEDIUM (I5 unbounded growth base). Owner-accepted limit. REVISIT TRIGGER: command_execution live rows above about 1M, or p95 executions-list latency above 200 ms, or a capped correlation reap on three consecutive passes. No-migration mitigations: skip the lookup for a slot already of token shape, add a created_at range predicate on the existing index, cache the immutable "execution is Forensics" fact, and raise or make the reap cap adaptive with a capped-pass alert. Stale comment on the existing alert calls the table lower stakes. No issue filed by this ledger. Also raised as: g8-perf-1 (performance, LOW), g8-arch-7.

summary: ROOT CAUSE SHARED BY SEVEN PASS 3 IDS (g8p3-cpx-1, g8p3-arch-1, g8p3-cps-1, g8p3-sec-1, g8p3-sre-1, g8-up3-1, g8p3-cons-2), introduced by the fix for g8-up-4 and g8-ch-1. The first form of that fix ran the Forensics execution lookup (a plain SELECT) on the upsert transaction's own connection, after the upsert and before the outbox append. A failed statement aborts a PostgreSQL transaction, so the lookup returned no answer, the text was reduced as intended, but the next statement (the outbox append) failed with an aborted-transaction error, the transaction rolled back and the agent's status was not recorded (the update is retried once and then logged as not recorded; agents do not re-send). Five reviewers reproduced the aborted-transaction behaviour on a disposable PostgreSQL 16; none ran the server binary against a faulted lookup. Because the guard compared against the sanitised form, the lookup also ran for every ordinary free-text failure frame (cost half: g8p3-sre-1b). Six reviewers (security-guardian, architect, cpp-expert, cpp-safety, sre, unhappy-path) derived it independently and none cites another; consistency-auditor and quality-engineer read the others first and are not counted. Fix in 92e0e60f5, read in the diff: the lookup runs only when the persisted text differs from the incoming text, under a SAVEPOINT rolled back on failure, so a failed lookup reduces the text while the status write, the outbox row and the bus event commit; the wiring gate pins the ingest-side reduction the skip relies on. The write-path fault case (g8p3-qe-2) was added in the same commit and 047b19be0 characterises the write path's trust in the ingest-reduced text. Primary row of the group. File and line are relative to 29af3e603 (1190). NOT verified: no governance agent has re-reviewed the fix; the SAVEPOINT release or rollback itself failing is logged only (not read as a hole by any reviewer); the sticky-terminal case still scans once inside the write transaction (g8p3-sre-1b). Fixed by: fix(tracker): a failed Forensics lookup can no longer lose an agent's status (92e0e60f5); test(tracker): characterise the write path's trust in the ingest-reduced text (047b19be0). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 3 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim.
